tools.description: Return stable application identity and runtime context, including versions, active profiles, and sharpit status. Use this before interpreting other results.
tools.name: get_overview

tools.description: Search effective configuration by name or displayed value and return a bounded result. Name search is relaxed-binding aware: it ignores case and treats `_` and `-` as `.`, so the dotted, kebab-case, and `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` spellings of one property all find it — `sharpit.mcp.enabled` also finds a value supplied as the environment variable `SHARPIT_MCP_ENABLED`, which is enumerated under that literal name. Values are matched literally, and each row reports the exact name and source its property source published. In `page`, `total` counts every property before filtering while `matched` counts the query hits, so `matched: 0` means this query found nothing, not that the property is absent — retry with a shorter query before concluding it is unset. Secret-like configuration values are masked; prefer a narrow query.
tools.name: get_config

tools.description: Search request routes and handlers and return a bounded result, including the application's effective `basePath` prefix when configured. Use a path, HTTP concept, or handler name as the query when locating an endpoint.
tools.name: get_mappings

tools.description: Search configured loggers by case-insensitive name and return their configured and effective levels, bounded by limit. Use to confirm actual logging levels before or after a code or configuration change.
tools.name: get_loggers

tools.description: Search FastAPI beans (dependency providers, middleware and the lifespan handler) by name or type and return a bounded result. Use this to verify runtime wiring, not as proof that a bean is exercised.
tools.name: get_beans

tools.description: Return a bounded, newest-first snapshot of the HTTP requests this application served: method, masked path and query, status, duration, response size and masked headers. sharpit's own requests are counted in `hiddenSelf`, not listed.
tools.name: get_http_exchanges

tools.description: Return the latest buffered application log snapshot, oldest first. Messages are masked at capture, but logs are application-controlled and may contain sensitive data; use them only in the local diagnostic context.
tools.name: get_log_tail

tools.description: List recent exception groups, newest first. Use a returned id with get_exception_detail for stack frames, causes, and individual occurrences. Without a caught-exceptions sensor, caughtInCode is null; insufficient and partial are evidence states, not findings. totalExceptions counts the occurrences in the retained groups, reset via CLI exceptions clear (clear_exceptions is refused over MCP).
tools.name: get_exceptions

tools.description: Return stack frames, causes, and occurrences for one exact exception-group id obtained from get_exceptions or get_live_activity.
tools.name: get_exception_detail

tools.description: Clear sharpit's bounded in-memory exception groups and occurrences. This does not suppress, handle, or change application exceptions.
tools.name: clear_exceptions

tools.description: Return the current bounded SQL trace snapshot with statements and timings. Application SQL may contain sensitive values; correlate it locally with request or trace identifiers.
tools.name: get_sql_traces

tools.description: Clear the bounded in-memory SQL trace buffer and return the resulting report. This does not execute SQL or change whether trace recording is enabled.
tools.name: clear_sql_traces

tools.description: Pause SQL trace recording and return the resulting report. Existing buffered traces remain available until explicitly cleared.
tools.name: pause_sql_trace_recording

tools.description: Resume SQL trace recording and return the resulting report. This only affects sharpit's bounded local capture and does not execute SQL.
tools.name: resume_sql_trace_recording

tools.description: Return a bounded, newest-first activity snapshot that merges HTTP requests, SQL statements and exceptions, correlated by request id. Use first when diagnosing one request.

tools.description: Return the cached health tree (database pings and the application's own checks) with each component's status and masked details. Never runs a check: an UNKNOWN status means the checks have not run yet.
tools.name: get_health

tools.description: Return each registered SQLAlchemy engine's connection pool: settings and live counters (checked out, idle, total). Reads counters only; never borrows a connection. A pool class that keeps no statistics is listed as unavailable.
tools.name: get_database_connection_pools

tools.description: Return this process's threads with inferred states (RUNNABLE or WAITING) and stacks, plus the event loop's asyncio tasks with their await chains and the request each one serves. `limit` caps both lists. Code names and line numbers only: no local variables or argument values.
tools.name: get_threads

tools.description: Return the cached vulnerability report, or the local dependency inventory before the first scan, without contacting OSV.dev or any other network service. Inspect `scan.status`, `scan.message`, `coverage` and `scan.packagesSkipped` before interpreting absent findings. Partial results retain available evidence; UNKNOWN severity is not zero risk. Coverage describes the inventory provider's accounting, not shaded-library discovery or exploitability. Lists vulnerable dependencies only unless `query` is given (default limit 10), at most 5 advisories each.
tools.name: get_vulnerabilities_report

tools.description: Actively query OSV.dev for known vulnerabilities in this application's dependencies and return severity-ranked findings. This sends package names/versions to OSV and, when enabled, CVE ids to FIRST for optional EPSS enrichment; run only with approval. Check `scan.status`, `scan.message`, `coverage` and `scan.packagesSkipped`: partial or unknown evidence is not a clean result, and inventory coverage does not prove reachability. Fixed versions are supported affected-interval candidates, not verified installable upgrades. Verify compatibility before changing a dependency. EPSS is the highest available per-CVE probability, not a combined probability or severity; optional enrichment failure retains OSV findings.
tools.name: vulnerabilities_scan

tools.description: Return the last completed REST API advisor report without starting a new endpoint scan. Use this cached evidence before deciding whether an active rest_api_scan is necessary. sampleViolations are bounded previews (up to 10), not the full violationCount. Use violationDetails.scanId with get_rest_api_rule_violations to page cached retained details without scanning again. Check truncated for missing details, including retention overflow; a terminal page does not guarantee completeness when truncated. Verify each finding before changing code.

tools.description: Read one page of retained violations for the exact rule id and cached report's violationDetails.scanId. This never starts a scan. Default offset 0 and limit 100; limit is capped at min(1000, transport max-results). Advance by page.returned while page.hasMore; page.total and page.matched count retained entries, not violationCount. If truncated, retention overflow or unavailable upstream details prevent a complete list. Verify each finding before changing code. Unknown rule returns 404; stale or missing snapshot returns 409: reread the cached report, not a new scan. On MCP -32003 byte-budget refusal, retry the same scanId and offset with a smaller limit; a refusal is not an empty or completed page.
tools.name: get_rest_api_rule_violations

tools.description: Actively inspect this application's routes and API design for correctness and maintainability risks. Use violationDetails.scanId with get_rest_api_rule_violations to page cached retained details without scanning again. Check truncated for missing details, including retention overflow; a terminal page does not guarantee completeness when truncated. Verify each finding before changing code.

tools.description: Return the HTTP routes this application served, grouped by method and route template, with request counts, status classes, errors and duration percentiles over the retained exchanges, ranked by requests, total time and p95 latency. A path no route matched is grouped by its masked path; query strings are never used.

tools.description: Open a profileable request or scheduled/message execution id from get_live_activity or a get_runtime_insights exemplar. Returns source=journal with the recorded timeline, route or execution label, authorizations, resources and touched metadata when retained, plus HTTP-exchange details when available; otherwise source=buffers with the HTTP-exchange profile (SQL N+1 groups, exceptionGroupId, and correlation tiers). An id neither retains is a tool error; available=false with source=none means the journal is off or the id cannot be profiled, and says why. Journal events follow panel visibility and exposure policy; do not infer absent work from a missing event. While relevant capture is held, lowFootprint identifies paused or partially paused evidence, not a quiet application; native statistics and Java-agent instrumentation may still run.
tools.name: get_request_profile

tools.description: Pause local transaction recording; existing entries remain available until cleared.

tools.description: Resume local transaction recording for new SQLAlchemy connection events.

tools.description: Actively read PostgreSQL's own pg_stat_* and pg_catalog views for the application datasources and record what the server currently reports: the live session snapshot, cache hit and rollback ratios, connection usage, transaction-ID age, the top normalized statements, index and relation activity, autovacuum state, replication and notable settings. This is a runtime view, not an advisor: it grades nothing and emits no findings. The read is bounded and read-only. Read every section's `reason` before trusting its rows: a section sharpit read only partly stays `AVAILABLE` and carries a non-null `reason`, so `status` alone does not mean complete, while `SKIPPED` and `FAILED` mark a section it did not read at all. A `hint` is a methodology caveat on rows that were read, not missing evidence. `truncated` means the row cap was reached, and any of these degrades the database and report `status` to `PARTIAL`. The usual cause is a role without pg_monitor membership, which hides other backends from the session list and the statement text and replica details from their sections. Budget exhaustion is reported in `reason`, not as row-cap truncation. An empty replica list proves absence only when `replication.replicasAvailable` is true; otherwise the list was not read. It answers with a summary, not the rows: status, message, readAt, truncated, and each database's status, message and sections (id, status, reason, rowCount, truncated). Read the rows, hints and replication details with get_postgresql_report, which returns this read without querying again.
tools.name: postgresql_read

tools.description: Return the last completed PostgreSQL runtime view without querying the server again. Before any read has run its `status` is `NOT_READ` and it carries no rows, which means nothing has been looked at rather than that nothing is wrong. Its session snapshot is only as current as that read, so prefer an active postgresql_read when the question is about what the database is doing right now. Check each section's `reason` for missing coverage; an empty replica list proves absence only when `replication.replicasAvailable` is true.
tools.name: get_postgresql_report

tools.description: Actively read MySQL's performance_schema and information_schema views for the application datasources and record what the server currently reports: the live session snapshot, the top normalized statements, index and relation activity, lock waits, replication channels, global status metrics and notable settings. This is a runtime view, not an advisor: it grades nothing and emits no findings. The read is bounded and read-only. Read every section's `reason` before trusting its rows: a section sharpit read only partly stays `AVAILABLE` and carries a non-null `reason`, so `status` alone does not mean complete, while `SKIPPED` and `FAILED` mark a section it did not read at all. A `hint` is a methodology caveat on rows that were read, not missing evidence. `truncated` means the row cap was reached, and any of these degrades the datasource and report `status` to `PARTIAL`. Budget exhaustion is reported in `reason`, not as row-cap truncation. It answers with a summary, not the rows: status, message, readAt, truncated, and each datasource's status, message and sections (id, status, reason, rowCount, truncated). Read the rows, hints and details with get_mysql_report, which returns this read without querying again.
tools.name: mysql_read

tools.description: Return the last completed MySQL runtime view without querying the server again. tools.description: Return stable application identity and runtime context, including versions, active profiles, and sharpit status. Use this before interpreting other results.
tools.name: get_overview

tools.description: Search effective configuration by name or displayed value and return a bounded result. Name search is relaxed-binding aware: it ignores case and treats `_` and `-` as `.`, so the dotted, kebab-case, and `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` spellings of one property all find it — `sharpit.mcp.enabled` also finds a value supplied as the environment variable `SHARPIT_MCP_ENABLED`, which is enumerated under that literal name. Values are matched literally, and each row reports the exact name and source its property source published. In `page`, `total` counts every property before filtering while `matched` counts the query hits, so `matched: 0` means this query found nothing, not that the property is absent — retry with a shorter query before concluding it is unset. Secret-like configuration values are masked; prefer a narrow query.
tools.name: get_config

tools.description: Search request routes and handlers and return a bounded result, including the application's effective `basePath` prefix when configured. Use a path, HTTP concept, or handler name as the query when locating an endpoint.
tools.name: get_mappings

tools.description: Search configured loggers by case-insensitive name and return their configured and effective levels, bounded by limit. Use to confirm actual logging levels before or after a code or configuration change.
tools.name: get_loggers

tools.description: Search FastAPI beans (dependency providers, middleware and the lifespan handler) by name or type and return a bounded result. Use this to verify runtime wiring, not as proof that a bean is exercised.
tools.name: get_beans

tools.description: Return a bounded, newest-first snapshot of the HTTP requests this application served: method, masked path and query, status, duration, response size and masked headers. sharpit's own requests are counted in `hiddenSelf`, not listed.
tools.name: get_http_exchanges

tools.description: Return the latest buffered application log snapshot, oldest first. Messages are masked at capture, but logs are application-controlled and may contain sensitive data; use them only in the local diagnostic context.
tools.name: get_log_tail

tools.description: List recent exception groups, newest first. Use a returned id with get_exception_detail for stack frames, causes, and individual occurrences. Without a caught-exceptions sensor, caughtInCode is null; insufficient and partial are evidence states, not findings. totalExceptions counts the occurrences in the retained groups, reset via CLI exceptions clear (clear_exceptions is refused over MCP).
tools.name: get_exceptions

tools.description: Return stack frames, causes, and occurrences for one exact exception-group id obtained from get_exceptions or get_live_activity.
tools.name: get_exception_detail

tools.description: Return the current bounded SQL trace snapshot with statements and timings. Application SQL may contain sensitive values; correlate it locally with request or trace identifiers.
tools.name: get_sql_traces

tools.description: Return a bounded, newest-first activity snapshot that merges HTTP requests, SQL statements and exceptions, correlated by request id. Use first when diagnosing one request.
tools.name: get_live_activity

tools.description: Return the Alembic migration history read from the revision files, oldest first, with each database's version as last read by the Alembic panel. Never connects to a database, imports a migration or runs env.py; `checkedAt` null means the database was not read yet.
tools.name: get_alembic_migrations

tools.description: Return the cached health tree (database pings and the application's own checks) with each component's status and masked details. Never runs a check: an UNKNOWN status means the checks have not run yet.
tools.name: get_health

tools.description: Return each registered SQLAlchemy engine's connection pool: settings and live counters (checked out, idle, total). Reads counters only; never borrows a connection. A pool class that keeps no statistics is listed as unavailable.
tools.name: get_database_connection_pools

tools.description: Return this process's threads with inferred states (RUNNABLE or WAITING) and stacks, plus the event loop's asyncio tasks with their await chains and the request each one serves. `limit` caps both lists. Code names and line numbers only: no local variables or argument values.
tools.name: get_threads

tools.description: Return the cached vulnerability report, or the local dependency inventory before the first scan, without contacting OSV.dev or any other network service. Inspect `scan.status`, `scan.message`, `coverage` and `scan.packagesSkipped` before interpreting absent findings. Partial results retain available evidence; UNKNOWN severity is not zero risk. Coverage describes the inventory provider's accounting, not shaded-library discovery or exploitability. Lists vulnerable dependencies only unless `query` is given (default limit 10), at most 5 advisories each.
tools.name: get_vulnerabilities_report

tools.description: Return the last completed REST API advisor report without starting a new endpoint scan. Use this cached evidence before deciding whether an active rest_api_scan is necessary. sampleViolations are bounded previews (up to 10), not the full violationCount. Use violationDetails.scanId with get_rest_api_rule_violations to page cached retained details without scanning again. Check truncated for missing details, including retention overflow; a terminal page does not guarantee completeness when truncated. Verify each finding before changing code.
tools.name: get_rest_api_report

tools.description: Read one page of retained violations for the exact rule id and cached report's violationDetails.scanId. This never starts a scan. Default offset 0 and limit 100; limit is capped at min(1000, transport max-results). Advance by page.returned while page.hasMore; page.total and page.matched count retained entries, not violationCount. If truncated, retention overflow or unavailable upstream details prevent a complete list. Verify each finding before changing code. Unknown rule returns 404; stale or missing snapshot returns 409: reread the cached report, not a new scan. On MCP -32003 byte-budget refusal, retry the same scanId and offset with a smaller limit; a refusal is not an empty or completed page.
tools.name: get_rest_api_rule_violations

tools.description: Return the HTTP routes this application served, grouped by method and route template, with request counts, status classes, errors and duration percentiles over the retained exchanges, ranked by requests, total time and p95 latency. A path no route matched is grouped by its masked path; query strings are never used.
tools.name: get_http_routes

tools.description: Open a profileable request or scheduled/message execution id from get_live_activity or a get_runtime_insights exemplar. Returns source=journal with the recorded timeline, route or execution label, authorizations, resources and touched metadata when retained, plus HTTP-exchange details when available; otherwise source=buffers with the HTTP-exchange profile (SQL N+1 groups, exceptionGroupId, and correlation tiers). An id neither retains is a tool error; available=false with source=none means the journal is off or the id cannot be profiled, and says why. Journal events follow panel visibility and exposure policy; do not infer absent work from a missing event. While relevant capture is held, lowFootprint identifies paused or partially paused evidence, not a quiet application; native statistics and Java-agent instrumentation may still run.
tools.name: get_request_profile

tools.description: Return the SQLAlchemy mapped classes passed to install(models=...) with their table, primary-key type and, once the application has configured its mappers, their relationships. Never configures mappers or runs SQL.
tools.name: get_data_repositories

tools.description: Return the newest bounded transaction snapshot captured from SQLAlchemy connection events. This reads only local cached data.
tools.name: get_transactions

tools.description: Return the last completed PostgreSQL runtime view without querying the server again. Before any read has run its `status` is `NOT_READ` and it carries no rows, which means nothing has been looked at rather than that nothing is wrong. Its session snapshot is only as current as that read, so prefer an active postgresql_read when the question is about what the database is doing right now. Check each section's `reason` for missing coverage; an empty replica list proves absence only when `replication.replicasAvailable` is true.
tools.name: get_postgresql_report

tools.description: Return the last completed MySQL runtime view without querying the server again. Before any read has run its `status` is `NOT_READ` and it carries no rows, which means nothing has been looked at rather than that nothing is wrong. Its session snapshot is only as current as that read, so prefer an active mysql_read when the question is about what the database is doing right now. Check each section's `reason` for missing coverage.
tools.name: get_mysql_report

tools.description: Return a newest-first list of the OpenTelemetry traces this application recorded: root span, HTTP path, services, epoch-nanosecond timing, span count and error/AI flags. Span attributes are masked. Requires the application's own OpenTelemetry SDK TracerProvider; sharpit never installs one.
